subject: Tenant ephemeral FQDN + SRV routing / mTLS rotation proposal for FinTrack private endpoints
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: FinTrack Security <security@fintrack.com>; Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@fintrack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant ephemeral FQDN + SRV routing / mTLS rotation proposal for FinTrack private endpoints

Hi Alice / FinTrack Sec team —

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment constraints yesterday. Based on our follow-up engineering review I wanted to propose a pragmatic architecture for per-tenant ephemeral endpoints that meets your no-public-DNS requirement while enabling zero-downtime cert rotation and weighted rollout across dedicated pools. High level:

- Scoped goal: allow FinTrack to route tenant traffic to Redwood-managed inference pools via private DNS while keeping control over client authentication (mTLS) and enabling short-lived leaf certs.
- Key constraints: no ACME/public CNAMEs; FinTrack must retain root trust for client identity; minimal changes to your existing private resolver ACLs.

Proposal (summary):
1) Ephemeral subdomains under FinTrack private zone: we'll create per-tenant aliases like _tf-tenant123._redwood.svc.fintrack.internal as SRV records. These SRV records point to service hostnames managed by Redwood (internal pool-IDs) and embed weight/priority for canary/burst routing.
2) Split-resolver delegation during rollouts: For a controlled cutover window, FinTrack creates NS delegations for a narrow subdomain (e.g. redwood.svc.fintrack.internal) to Redwood's private Resolver endpoint (IP ranges we provide). This is time-limited and scoped; we provide a CSV (attached) for the exact NS entries.
3) mTLS model: FinTrack keeps the root CA for client certs. Redwood will run a short-lived leaf cert issuance flow: customers pre-approve scoped CSRs via your ops team (signed by your private CA), or optionally we can accept a signed intermediate you mint for Redwood (your preference). We prefer the intermediate path when you can allow it — reduces operational friction.
4) Rotation without downtime: rotate certs by issuing new leaf certs with overlapping validity and perform SRV weight flips at the TTL boundary. TTLs will be aggressive (10s–30s) during rollout windows; we orchestrate weight change in a staged fashion: 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
5) Revocation/incident path: we maintain a short-lived OCSP responder inside the private network (details in runbook). In emergencies we can instantly reduce SRV weights to 0 for any pool and failover to a fallback internal pool.

Attachments: runbook (detailed flows), zone-delegation-request.csv (NS records), ROTATION diagram.

Open questions for FinTrack:
- Do you prefer Redwood to hold a short-lived intermediate signed by your CA, or do you want the CSR-by-review flow for each tenant leaf cert?
- Are there any internal restrictions on creating SRV records of the _redwood.* subdomain?
- Confirm acceptable TTL lower bound — we recommend 15s for controlled windows; if your resolver throttles sub-second updates we can adjust.

Next steps: if you approve the approach we can run a dry-run with a non-production tenant next week. Ben / Marissa — can you confirm if this approach requires any infra changes on Redwood side (pool naming, weight API exposure)?

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@fintrack.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTrack Security <security@fintrack.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant ephemeral FQDN + SRV routing / mTLS rotation proposal for FinTrack private endpoints

Irene — thanks for the summary, this is helpful. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Root trust: we cannot create an intermediate CA for an external vendor. Our policy requires the root to remain strictly under our control; we can however sign short-lived intermediates (24–72h) with an automated approval flow.
2) SRV usage: our infra team is fine with a dedicated _redwood.* subtree, but we cannot do global NS delegation for broad names. The CSV approach scoped to redwood.svc.fintrack.internal during the rollout window sounds acceptable — we'll need the exact TTLs and the IP list in advance.
3) OCSP + auditing: we'll want full audit logs for certificate issuance (CSR -> signed cert) and a signed artifact we can ingest into our audit pipeline. Can Redwood emit a signed issuance record per cert (JSON + signature) that we can push into our SIEM?

If you can provide a short checklist for the CSR-by-review flow (who at FinTrack signs, what approval email patterns look like) we can run the dry-run.

-Alice
Security Ops 
FinTrack

Team — forwarding FinTrack's reply and their constraints. Action items: 

- Ben: can Redwood support the CSR-by-review flow (they will sign short-lived intermediates automatically, but won't mint a long-lived intermediate for us). We need tooling to accept pre-signed intermediate certs (24–72h validity) and use them to sign leaf certs, plus generate an issuance artifact (signed JSON) per cert for FinTrack's SIEM.
- Laura: audit logs — do we have an existing issuance-event signer (HSM-backed)? If not, what's the minimal implementation to produce a signed JSON record per issuance that includes CSR fingerprint, tenant ID, issued_at, expiry, issuer_fingerprint?
- Marissa: operational notes — we need to publish a one-page CSR checklist for FinTrack (who signs, acceptance email pattern, required CN/SAN formats). Also confirm the ability to set dynamic SRV weights via our routing API and a recommended TTL window (we recommended 15s).

I've attached the runbook and the CSV they requested. Suggest we sync for 30m tomorrow to align on scope before the dry-run.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Tenant ephemeral FQDN + SRV routing / mTLS rotation proposal for FinTrack private endpoints

Thanks — we can support this. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) CSR-by-review flow: our cert service can ingest pre-signed intermediates for short windows. We'll add a verification step: the intermediate must include an x509 extension with "redwood-allowed: true" and be delivered over a signed SFTP drop or the private control plane. I'll own the implementation. ETA: 8 business days for the ingestion endpoint and automation (INF-3921).

2) Issuance artifact: Laura confirms we can produce an HSM-signed JSON issuance record with the fields Alice requested. It will be timestamped and include HMAC and cert fingerprint; output will be S3 (private region) + push to your SIEM webhook. Laura — please note HSM quota and we may need a short exception for higher throughput during dry-runs.

3) SRV weight API & TTLs: Marissa confirms the routing API has a weight flip endpoint. For the dry-run we will use 30s TTL and a staged rollout script (attached in runbook). We will provide the exact NS/IP list in the CSV once infra schedules the resolver ACL change.

4) Dry-run plan: schedule for Tue next week 11am PT. We'll do a non-prod tenant, perform the CSR-by-review issuance, delegate the tiny redwood subdomain for 1 hour, and run the weighted flip 10%->50%->100% over 20 minutes. We'll capture issuance artifacts and provide logs to FinTrack.

I'll kick off the INF ticket and loop Laura/Marissa for the HSM artifact work.

-Ben
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
